projects.title: OpenTESArena
projects.status: Work in progress; the project README describes core exploration, combat, shops, citizens, and travel systems, while quests, spells, saving, and loading remain incomplete.
projects.summary: Clean-room C++ reimplementation of The Elder Scrolls: Arena. It does not distribute the original game data; users provide their own files.
projects.source_available: Public C++ source repository; original Arena game data required and not included

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: clean-room scope, current features, platforms, and required data

projects.title: OpenEnroth
projects.game: Might and Magic VII: For Blood and Honor
projects.status: Active development; Might and Magic VII is the playable target, while VI and VIII are planned. Nightly builds are documented; an original game installation is required.
projects.summary: Open-source C++ reimplementation of the Might and Magic VI–VIII engine family. The README identifies Might and Magic VII as the playable game and says the other two titles are planned.
projects.strategy: Native engine reimplementation from reverse engineering
projects.source_available: Public C++ source repository and nightly builds; original game data required
projects.subtype: Multi-title engine project; Might and Magic VII currently playable

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: game scope, status, platforms, and data requirements

projects.title: OpenCrystalCaves
projects.status: Episode 1 is playable; the project reimplements the Crystal Caves trilogy and requires original game data for episodes not included with the shareware release.
projects.summary: Open-source C++20 reimplementation of the Crystal Caves game engine and trilogy. The repository provides the shareware episode; other original game data is not included.
projects.source_available: Public C++ source repository; shareware episode is included and other original game data is required

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: trilogy scope, playable episode, platforms, and data distribution

projects.title: OpenGothic
projects.game: Gothic II: Night of the Raven
projects.status: The maintainer describes the Gothic II client as feature-complete and reports that the main quest and expansion can be completed. Gothic I is not an officially supported target; original game data is required.
projects.summary: Open-source C++ reimplementation of the Gothic II engine and client. It runs the original game data and does not include the commercial assets.
projects.source_available: Public C++ source repository; user-supplied Gothic II game data required

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: supported game, completion status, platforms, and data requirements

projects.title: OpenLara: Classic Tomb Raider Engine
projects.platform: DOS/Windows → WebGL, Windows/Linux/macOS, Android/iOS, and documented console ports (support varies)
projects.status: Active source project with a WebGL demo and standalone builds; platform-specific ports and binaries have different release dates and support levels.
projects.summary: Open-source C/C++ engine reimplementation for the classic Tomb Raider games. It uses game data supplied by the player and offers a browser demo plus platform-specific builds.
projects.strategy: Native engine reimplementation and multi-platform source port
projects.source_available: Public source repository; original Tomb Raider game data required for full game content
projects.subtype: Multi-title game engine; platform ports vary in maintenance and completeness

sources.label: Maintainer repository README and release list: engine scope, WebGL demo, and platform targets

projects.title: OpenUG2
projects.status: Early prototype; the README documents asset loading, rendering, driving, and races, with only selected content verified. This is not a complete or drop-in game replacement.
projects.summary: Clean-room C/C++ engine prototype for Need for Speed: Underground 2. It reads the user’s original game data and does not include EA code or assets.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied Need for Speed: Underground 2 data required

sources.label: Maintainer repository README and roadmap: clean-room scope, prototype features, platforms, and data requirements

projects.title: OpenRealm
projects.status: Experimental open-source engine; Warcraft III is the primary playable target. The README identifies other game support as exploratory and requires user-supplied MPQ data.
projects.summary: C-based native engine reimplementation for Warcraft III, with client/server, map scripting, campaign, and multiplayer systems. It reads the user’s MPQ files and does not include Blizzard assets.
projects.source_available: Public C source repository; user-supplied Warcraft III MPQ files required
projects.subtype: Warcraft III engine reimplementation; other titles are exploratory

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: supported game, systems, platforms, and MPQ requirements

projects.title: OpenGold: Pool of Radiance Reimplementation
projects.status: Work in progress; the maintainer documents playable New Phlan and Slums areas, with the full campaign incomplete. Windows and macOS instructions are present.
projects.summary: C++20/Godot-based reimplementation of the Pool of Radiance game engine. It reads original game data that is not distributed with the project.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; original Pool of Radiance game data required and not included
projects.subtype: Role-playing game engine reimplementation; campaign incomplete

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: project identity, implementation, playable areas, and data requirements

projects.title: The Force Engine: Dark Forces
projects.status: Dark Forces is reported playable from beginning to end. The engine requires the original commercial game data; Outlaws is a separate, incomplete target.
projects.summary: Native C++ reverse-engineered replacement for the Jedi engine used by Dark Forces. It is a new engine implementation, not an emulator, and does not include the commercial game data.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; original Dark Forces game data required
projects.subtype: Native game engine replacement; Dark Forces supported, Outlaws incomplete

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: engine scope, Dark Forces completeness, platforms, and data requirements

projects.title: MDK SDL
projects.status: The project README marks the game playable level by level. Windows gameplay has been tested; Linux/macOS builds are covered by CI, and Android controls remain in progress.
projects.summary: C# / SDL3 reverse-engineered native implementation of MDK. It requires the user’s original game data, which is not included; the repository also documents an Android APK.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineered native game reimplementation using SDL3
projects.source_available: Public C# source repository; original MDK game data required and not included

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: project method, playability, platforms, and required data

projects.title: OpenSims2
projects.status: Work in progress; the macOS build reaches neighborhood selection and lots. The README limits support to the base game; expansions are unsupported.
projects.summary: Native C++/Metal engine reimplementation of The Sims 2 for Apple Silicon Macs. It asks users to provide their own game folder and does not distribute game files.
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied Sims 2 base-game files required
projects.subtype: macOS-native engine reimplementation; base game only

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: supported game, build requirements, current progress, and data requirements

projects.title: OpenFodder
projects.platform: Amiga/PC → Windows/Linux/BSD/other Unix-like systems and WebGL demos
projects.status: Released native engine/source port; the project reports support for six Amiga demos and three retail releases. The official site offers playable browser demos and the project publishes desktop builds.
projects.summary: Open-source C++ engine reimplementation/source port for Cannon Fodder. The engine is GPL-licensed; players provide original retail game data, while separately distributed shareware demos are available.
projects.strategy: Native engine reimplementation and source port
projects.source_available: Public GPL source repository; retail game data is user-supplied and demos are separately available
projects.subtype: Multi-release engine reimplementation with browser demos

sources.label: Maintainer repository README: supported releases, licensing, platforms, and data policy
Official project site: browser demos and current desktop release
